items.title: One look for every stat
items.body: Session cards, Week, Month and the monitor's stats now match the Day summary: the label on top, the unit beside the number, and no data in words when a value is missing.

items.title: New home page and changelog
items.body: The home page has a cleaner layout, newer screenshots and a stream preview at true size. Every update since launch now has its own page you can filter, and the privacy page is finished.

items.title: Tidier monitor controls
items.body: Stop, posture, the Log row and live sharing now sit in one Controls section, closed until you need it, and its header still shows your posture and whether you are live. Switches, buttons and fields match the rest of aorti.

items.title: Saved sessions show first
items.body: The viewer opens straight to what you saw last, then checks Drive quietly in the background. It only redraws if something actually changed.

items.title: Correct session lengths
items.body: Some sessions showed impossible lengths, like 70 hours. Times now come from the real clock in each file, and a new web session always starts its own clock.

items.title: Arrange your Trends
items.body: Pick which Trends cards show and drag them into your own order. Each one can be half or full width.

items.title: Smoother zooming
items.body: Scrolling and zooming the Day chart is much lighter on phones and laptops. On touch, pinch or double-tap to zoom; on a laptop, drag across the chart to zoom to that stretch.

items.title: Tidier Day view
items.body: The date now opens a calendar for picking another day, and one Layers list turns chart lines on or off. Markers open in a drawer that no longer squeezes the chart.

items.title: Bubble stays on screen
items.body: The floating bubble can no longer be dragged or rotated partly off the edge of the screen.

items.title: Day view explorer
items.body: The Day view now shows the whole day on one chart you can explore. Marks show as diamonds you can edit or delete, and sleep start and end can be marked by hand.

items.title: Phone viewer shows your data
items.body: The viewer in the app could open empty on some phones. It now shows your saved summaries right away and refreshes them in the background.

items.title: Log a symptom or a note
items.body: A Log row lets you mark a symptom or jot a quick note during a session. Both show on the Day view at that minute.

items.title: Symptom from the notification
items.body: The recording notification has a Symptom button for marking a moment. Its status now reads in hours and minutes.

items.title: Choose when to sync
items.body: On the web, Drive sync is now a setting you can turn off. After you stop, the monitor says where the session was saved and links straight to it.

items.title: Bubble closes with the session
items.body: The floating bubble closes by itself once no session is running. Its stop icon is easier to see.

items.title: Recording comes back on its own
items.body: If Android closes the app while you record, the session picks back up by itself, in the same file, usually within a few seconds.

items.title: Reconnects when back in range
items.body: Walk away from your phone and the notification says the strap is reconnecting. Come back and recording picks up again by itself, with no need to open the app.

items.title: Hourly files on Drive
items.body: Sessions now also save as small hourly files in a folder for each month on your Drive. Each finished hour uploads once, so syncing is faster.

items.title: Refreshed stream widget
items.body: The widget has a new font and clearer warning colours, and a warning keeps flashing until it clears. The OBS source now matches the monitor preview at the same size.

items.title: Faster sync, no duplicate files
items.body: Sync no longer reads every saved session again, and a resumed session no longer leaves a second copy on Drive.

items.title: No more stuck restore screen
items.body: Coming back to the app no longer shows a spinner for up to a minute, and Stop responds right away, even on a weak connection. Long sessions ask before stopping.

items.title: No more hanging on restore
items.body: In rare cases the app could sit on Restoring session until you force-closed it. It now finishes or gives up within about a minute.

items.title: Overlay stays live all session
items.body: Late in long sessions the stream overlay and Watch live could stop updating. They now keep going for the whole session.

items.title: Safer sign-in on the phone
items.body: Sign-in details are stored more securely on the phone, and live data from other devices is checked before it shows.

items.title: No double stream on reopen
items.body: Reopening the app while you share live no longer starts a second copy of your stream.

items.title: More dependable Drive sync
items.body: Sync now waits for an upload to land before it says it is done, and new data shows in the viewer right after. Sync messages are plainer too.

items.title: Floating heart rate bubble
items.body: A long press on the widget pops your heart rate into a bubble that floats over other apps. A tap switches it between a compact view and a card with HRV.

items.title: Markers on the right day
items.body: Markers from sessions that cross midnight now land on the correct day.

items.title: Full 24-hour day chart
items.body: The Day chart now runs midnight to midnight, and sessions longer than a day show on every day they cover. Early-morning sessions no longer slip to the day before.

items.title: Keeps recording overnight
items.body: Android is much less likely to stop a recording overnight. If it does, the app brings it back on its own.

items.title: Choose your summary stats
items.body: Pick which numbers show in a session summary from its menu. SDNN is now one of the options.

items.title: Faster charts
items.body: The viewer redraws far less, so charts scroll and resize smoothly. Zoomed-out charts keep their highs and lows, so they match the summary numbers.

items.title: Try the viewer with sample data
items.body: Open Sample data in the menu to see what the viewer looks like with two weeks of sample sessions. No sign-in needed.

items.title: Plays nicely with Sleep As Android
items.body: aorti can share your strap with sleep-tracking apps. No need to disconnect one to use the other.

items.title: Mobile reliability fixes
items.body: Recovers better from brief strap drops, including overnight. Long sessions use less battery.

items.title: Viewer tweaks
items.body: The chills sensitivity slider filters events properly. Sundays open in the week view, and HR shifts show in purple so they do not look like chills.

items.title: Save CSV anywhere
items.body: Tapping Export CSV opens a save dialog, so the file goes wherever you pick.

items.title: Record without signing in
items.body: You can record without a Google account; sessions stay on the phone. Old ones are cleared before storage runs low, and you can clear them yourself.

items.title: Swipe to stop
items.body: Ending a session is now a swipe, so a stray tap will not stop it. Stop in the notification works again.

items.title: Fewer false alerts
items.body: Chills and flushing alerts were rewritten and fire far less often on ordinary changes in heart rate.

items.title: Late-night sessions split by day
items.body: A session that runs past midnight now shows its part on each day instead of all on the day it started.

items.title: Now called aorti
items.body: The app has a new name and a home at aorti.ca. You can sign in right from the home page.

items.title: Steadier strap connection
items.body: The Android app was rebuilt to hold a steadier connection to your strap, so readings no longer go quiet mid-session.

items.title: Record in the background
items.body: Start a session on Android and it keeps recording with the screen off. A settings shortcut helps stop your phone from closing it to save battery.

items.title: Skipped-beat detection
items.body: The monitor flags beats that look skipped or early, with a slider to set how sensitive it is.

items.title: Reports by day, week and month
items.body: The viewer turns your sessions into plain-English reports with noteworthy moments called out. It syncs both ways with Google Drive.

items.title: Heart rate on your stream
items.body: Add the overlay as a browser source in OBS and it mirrors the widget on your monitor as you change its settings. Watch live shows the same view on any other screen.
